title: Modernizing Spectrum Sharing for Satellite Broadband (Report and Order, FCC 26-26, SB Docket No. 25-157)
key_claim: The FCC adopts a Report and Order revising the GSO/NGSO spectrum-sharing framework, replacing mandatory Equivalent Power Flux Density (EPFD) limits with a coordination-based framework backed by performance-based GSO protection criteria; rules effective 13 July 2026.
notes: Primary regulator filing. Tier 1 anchor for the spectrum-rule change underpinning the signal.

publisher: First Responder Network Authority (US Department of Commerce / NTIA)
title: 3GPP completes Release 19, while progress begins on 6G work
key_claim: US government agency confirms 3GPP Release 19 specifications were declared frozen at the December 2025 plenary, including completed work items for NTN for NR, IoT NTN and LTE-to-NR-NTN mobility; Release 20 carries integration of NTN into the 5G architecture and 6G NTN operation on terrestrial-network bands.
notes: Primary government-agency confirmation of the standards milestone embedding satellite into mainstream mobile specifications.

title: Next-gen satellite internet is transforming pricing, capacity, and regulation worldwide (TMT Predictions 2026)
key_claim: D2D can connect the unconnected via a flurry of MNO-satellite partnerships and fast-moving spectrum allocation, but monetisation remains elusive; regulators and standards bodies have moved quickly to accommodate non-terrestrial networks.
notes: Structural anchor (3-6m band): canonical institutional framing of the D2D commercial-and-regulatory inflection. Also anchors the counter-argument on monetisation.

title: Policy Reforms to Launch US Space Innovation
key_claim: US competitiveness in the space economy depends on aggressive regulatory modernisation, including making FCC spectrum more readily available; without comprehensive reform the US risks falling behind in the global race to lead space innovation.
notes: Think-tank framing of the policy-competition logic driving the FCC's spectrum liberalisation.

title: GSMA Calls for Regulatory Readiness for Direct-to-User LEO Satellite Services (position paper: Regulatory Preparedness for Satellite Services)
key_claim: GSMA urges policymakers to establish 'regulatory parity' so that satellite providers face the same legal and regulatory obligations as mobile operators, and to safeguard national sovereignty as LEO D2D services scale.
notes: Global mobile-industry institution; primary policy research. Direct evidence that the mobile industry sees satellite operators acquiring asymmetric rights.

title: FCC Approves Landmark Spectrum Sharing and Direct-to-Device Frameworks
key_claim: SpaceX is approved to acquire ~65 MHz of mid-band spectrum (AWS-3, AWS-4, H-Block) from EchoStar for $17bn; FCC replaces terrestrial buildout requirements with space-based buildout conditions; transaction consummation expected by 30 November 2027.
notes: Trade-press account of the SpaceX-EchoStar spectrum transfer and the broader May 2026 FCC package.

title: Convergence Comes of Age: 2026 Shifts Satellite Promise into Commercial Reality
key_claim: D2D is forecast as a $30bn revenue opportunity for telecoms operators by 2035; vertically integrated players such as Starlink (9,400 satellites) hold a structural advantage, and a wave of satellite M&A is consolidating the field; satellites will complement rather than replace terrestrial networks.
notes: Authored by GSMA Intelligence's head of research. Anchors the consolidation/vertical-integration thread and part of the counter-argument.

title: D2D satellite set to dominate WRC-27 agenda
key_claim: D2D (termed 'DC-MSS-IMT' in the ITU context) is fast-tracked onto the WRC-27 agenda in Shanghai (Oct-Nov 2027), where up to 80% of the agenda touches satellite issues; national regulators including Ofcom are running interim D2D licensing through MNO licences pending international rules.
notes: Trade-press account of the international-spectrum dimension and the regulatory improvisation underway ahead of WRC-27.
